If you can't fix every distortion, should you fix one?

Why do governments fail when politicians follow their incentives?

Which efficiency matters more in the long run?

Test: do markets work?

Do people care about fairness?
Why tip a waiter you will never see again?

Can economics explain marriage and children?
Can economics explain suicide?
Why vote when your vote almost never matters?
Is "rational choice" a theory or a tautology?
Who are you — and does it change what you choose?
Does culture shape economic choices?
Is attention a scarce resource?

Why are some firms so much more productive than others?
Where do new firms come from, and why do most die?
Why do platforms win so big?

quiz.question: Country A grows 1% a year, country B 3%. Both start at $2,000 a head. After 70 years, roughly how many times richer is B than A?
A poor country manages 7% growth a year. Roughly how many years until its income per person doubles?
A student could earn $20,000 a year in a job. Instead she studies, paying $8,000 a year in fees. What does a year of study cost her?
A surgeon earning $300 an hour and a student earning $15 an hour each queue two hours for free festival tickets. For whom is the free ticket dearer?
Which of these is economics?
choices: Bread and the tip: money changes hands

quiz.question: A city doubles its parking fine but halves its patrols, so a ticket is half as likely. In Becker's simplest model, what happens to illegal parking?
On 3 September 1967 all of Sweden switched overnight from driving on the left to driving on the right. Which answer explains the switch most simply?
choices: A new rule moved everyone's best choice
Drivers had come to prefer the right
Driving on the right got cheaper

quiz.question: A traffic model treats every driver as identical and perfectly informed, and has predicted rush-hour jams well for ten years. What would Friedman say?
choices: Keep using it: it predicts well

quiz.question: The city now brings in a congestion toll. Why might the same traffic model start to fail?
choices: Drivers change routes and times in ways it ignored

quiz.question: A model of Harbourtown's fishing grounds assumes every fisher catches the same amount. Which question does that assumption most endanger?
choices: How the fish price moves after a storm
Who in town gets richest from fishing
Whether a storm cuts the total catch

quiz.question: Mia is better at both jobs. Can trading with Jon still make her better off?
choices: No, he has nothing she needs

quiz.question: A surgeon types faster than her assistant. Who should type her letters?
In a day Ana makes 6 shirts or 3 tables; Ben makes 2 shirts or 2 tables. Who should make the tables?
choices: Ana: she is better at both

quiz.question: Making a car costs Freeland 3 tons of wheat, and Agraria 5 tons. At which price can both gain when Freeland sells cars for wheat?
Why does a diamond cost more than a glass of water?
choices: Diamonds take more work to dig out
It depends on how much of each we already have

quiz.question: Harbourtown's reservoir runs low and water is rationed. What happens to what people would pay for one more litre?
choices: It stays the same: water is just as useful

quiz.question: Labs learn to grow diamonds identical to mined ones, cheaply and in any number. What happens to the price of a diamond?
choices: It falls toward the cost of growing one
It stays high: diamonds are still beautiful
It rises: more people can now get one

quiz.question: Air is more useful than water or diamonds, yet it is free. Why?
choices: One more breath is worth nothing when air is everywhere
The government sets its price at zero

quiz.question: Crates are left over at $7. Which way will the price move?
Concert tickets sell out in minutes and are resold for three times the price. What does that tell you about the original price?
Where would you expect the price of the same old lamp to vary more from one sale to the next?
choices: A flea market where each buyer haggles alone
An auction room where everyone hears every bid

quiz.question: A storm keeps Harbourtown's fishing boats in port for a week. What happens to the price of fish and the amount sold?
A summer festival fills Harbourtown with mainland visitors. What happens at Mia's bakery?
Bread gets dearer, and Harbourtown families buy less bread. What is that, for the families?
choices: A move along their demand curve

quiz.question: A cheaper oven cuts Mia's costs just as a sourdough craze sweeps the town. What can we say for sure?
A cap holds the price below where supply and demand now meet. What happens?
A frost destroys 5% of the world's coffee crop. Drinkers barely change their habits for months, and new bushes take years to grow. The price will most likely…
Ten years after an oil cut, people have bought efficient cars and new oil fields have opened. An equal second cut would raise the price…
How much does this add to Harbourtown's GDP?
A carpenter buys wood for $300 and sells the table for $800. How much does the carpenter's work add to GDP?
Country X's income per person is $4,000 at market exchange rates, and its prices are about half America's. Roughly what is it at PPP?
A government wants to know how many foreign-made vaccines its economy could pay for. Which measure fits?
Norway puts most of its oil income into a fund instead of spending it. On Jones and Klenow's welfare measure, Norway looks…
choices: about as rich as its GDP

quiz.question: After a hurricane, a town spends a year rebuilding the houses it lost. What happens to its GDP that year?
Flour got dearer and a cheap rival opened, both in the same month. What can we say for sure about Mia's bread?
A new harbour crane lets the same crews land twice the fish. What happens on the picture?
choices: The town slides along the frontier
The town moves inside the frontier

quiz.question: Ola can make 4 nets or 2 oars in a day; Sara 1 net or 1 oar. Who should make the oars?
choices: Nobody gains from splitting the work

quiz.question: When economists say a market 'works', which test do they usually mean first?
Two economists agree that a congestion charge would cut city traffic by a fifth and hit poorer drivers hardest. One backs it, the other opposes it. What is the most likely reason?
choices: One of them has the facts wrong
They weigh efficiency and fairness differently
One of them doesn't understand markets

quiz.question: A city's taxi market is congested and overpriced. Is that enough to justify the city running the taxis itself?
choices: Yes: a failing market justifies stepping in
Not by itself: how well the city would run them must be compared too

quiz.question: Harbourtown's ferry raises its fares by 10%, and trips fall by 4%. What happens to the ferry's fare takings?
A city doubles its downtown parking fees. When is the drop in car trips biggest?
Smokers barely cut back when cigarettes cost more; tobacco firms can easily sell elsewhere. Who bears most of a cigarette tax?
Parliament moves the whole payroll tax from employers to workers' payslips. Once wages adjust, what does the simple model predict for take-home pay?
Wikipedia is free to read. What does its zero price tell us about what readers gain from it?
choices: Nothing: the gain is its worth above a zero price
Readers gain nothing, since they pay nothing
The gain equals the donations it receives

quiz.question: A concert sells out at $60 a ticket. Which buyer gains least?
choices: The fan who would have paid $200
The fan who would have paid just $60

quiz.question: The harbour council asks what a new ferry is worth to Harbourtown. Which number comes closest?
choices: Riders' value above the fare, plus the operator's margin over cost

quiz.question: Double the tax from $1 to $2. Roughly how many times bigger does the deadweight loss get?
A city doubles its hotel tax from $5 to $10 a night. Roughly what happens to the deadweight loss?
Which tax wastes least?
choices: A tax on one brand of cola

quiz.question: A country taxes imported bananas so heavily that nobody imports any. The tax raises nothing. What does it cost?
choices: The bananas people no longer get to eat
Exactly what it would have raised

quiz.question: Harbourtown's council caps the fee for a harbour mooring at half the market fee. What follows?
A city caps rents at $3,000 a month where the market rent is $2,000. What happens?
A hard rent cap stays in place for ten years. Compared with year one, the shortage is…
Which design protects sitting tenants while giving landlords the least reason to stop renting?
choices: Government pays part of a sitting tenant's large rent rise
A hard cap on every rent
The cap extended to new buildings

quiz.question: A country sets a minimum price for wheat below what wheat sells for anyway. What happens?
Before 1978, US regulators kept air fares high and airlines could not undercut them. What would you expect to see?
A minimum price for milk, and nobody buys up what is left over. Which farmers gain?
What does the cannery need to know before it uses less tin?
choices: Which of the two causes it was
Where the tin is needed most
Only that tin now costs more

quiz.question: Copper suddenly gets dearer, and an electrician switches some jobs to aluminium wire without knowing why. Which fits Hayek?
choices: She is doing the right thing without knowing the cause
She should wait until she knows the cause
Only a planner could tell her to switch

quiz.question: A factory dumps its waste into a river for free. What is wrong with the price of what it makes?
choices: It says the product is cheaper to make than it really is
Nothing: a price always carries the full cost

quiz.question: A concert sells tickets at $50, though fans would pay $300, and resale is banned. What decides who gets in?
choices: Nothing: fans just get a bargain

quiz.question: A city makes downtown parking free. Where does the gap go?
choices: Into time spent circling for a space

quiz.question: After a flood, every household gets a water coupon, and coupons may be sold. Compared with one long queue, what changes?
choices: Those who need less sell to those who need more, and no time is lost queuing

quiz.question: A dollar for every fish landed: does the total gain grow or shrink?
Random bids, plus that one rule. How much of the possible gain did these traders capture?
Concert tickets resell in an open market that settles at $80 a ticket. Who ends up with the tickets?
choices: Those who value a ticket above $80

quiz.question: A competitive bread market is efficient. Does that mean every hungry family gets bread?
choices: Yes: efficiency means nobody goes without
No: it counts what people can pay, not what they need

quiz.question: Liv has six fish, Tor has two, and two lie on the quay. Which move is a Pareto improvement?
choices: Liv gives Tor one of hers
Split all ten, five and five

quiz.question: Liv has all ten fish and Tor has none. Is that split Pareto efficient?
Liv has three fish, Tor has three, and four rot on the quay. Which split is a Pareto improvement on that?
choices: Six for Liv, two for Tor
Three for Liv, seven for Tor
Nine for Liv, one for Tor

quiz.question: A concert hall sells 80 of its 100 seats. Twenty stay empty, while fans outside would gladly sit in them. Pareto efficient?
choices: Yes, every buyer got a seat
No, a seat could go to a fan and nobody loses

quiz.question: A king owns all the land, his subjects own none, and every field is farmed. Pareto efficient?
choices: It can be: any change takes land from the king
No, the subjects could be better off

quiz.question: A new road saves drivers $10 million a year and costs the farmers whose land it crosses $2 million. Nobody pays the farmers. What is it?
Two neighbours, one growing only tomatoes and the other only beans, swap until neither can gain without the other losing. What have they reached?
choices: The one deal a market would pick

quiz.question: Two traders reach a deal where any further swap would hurt one of them. Is that deal fair?
A buyer and a seller haggle over a used bike. Any price from $80 to $120 leaves both better off. Which prices give an efficient outcome?
choices: Any price in that range, if the bike changes hands

quiz.question: Before taxes and transfers, how unequal is the US compared with France, Germany and Belgium?
In the same survey, what share of Americans said the poor are lazy?
In 2022 Finland's Gini before taxes and transfers was 51, the same as America's. After them it was 27. What best explains the gap?
A party promises to move a country from US-style to Belgian-style shares with no loss of output. What does that promise most need evidence for?
choices: That the new point is efficient

quiz.question: A country pays every adult $1,000 a year, no conditions, and funds it with an income tax. Which part changes what an extra hour of work pays?
Two towns raise the same money: one with a flat fee per household, one with a 30% tax on earnings. Where do people work more?
Plan X gives the richer group 10 and the poorer 2. Plan Y gives 6 and 5. Which does a Rawlsian pick?
A plan raises the richer group from 8 to 10 and leaves the poorer at 3. What does a strict Rawlsian rule say?
A utilitarian can give $100 to a millionaire or to a family scraping by. Each extra dollar matters less the more you have. Which adds more wellbeing?
Land was seized from its owners a century ago, then sold on in fair, voluntary sales ever since. By Nozick's test, is today's owner's title just?
choices: Yes: every recent sale was voluntary
No: the chain starts with a theft

quiz.question: Society X: poorest 12, average 80. Society Y: poorest 18, average 60. Which does Rawls's maximin pick?
Same two societies. A group insists nobody falls below 10, then maximises the average. X or Y?
Which of these could an experiment settle?
choices: What people choose behind a veil

quiz.question: A city caps taxi licences at 500, and a licence sells for a fortune. Which assumption of perfect competition fails?
Mia's bakery is the only one in Harbourtown that bakes sourdough. Which assumptions fail?
One firm makes 40% of all the cement in a region. Why might it produce less than where P = MC?
choices: Extra cement would lower the price of all it sells
Cement costs a lot to make

quiz.question: A town caps food-truck licences at ten, and they trade at $80,000 each. You buy one. What economic profit can you expect?
choices: About zero: the licence price absorbed it

quiz.question: Demand for film-camera repairs collapses, and repair shops start losing money. What happens in the long run?
choices: Shops keep losing money for good
Some close, until those left earn a normal profit

quiz.question: Where does a profit-seeking yard produce?
A town's only theatre sells 100 seats at $30, or 110 if it cuts the price to $28 for everyone. What do the extra 10 seats add to revenue?
Cheaper ingredients cut a patented drug's marginal cost. What does its one-price monopolist do?
choices: Keeps the price and pockets the saving
Cuts the price and sells more

quiz.question: A city has one licence for an airport bus. Which way of handing it out wastes the least?
choices: Auction it; the money goes to the city
Give it to the firm that lobbies hardest
Let firms compete with ads and studies for a year

quiz.question: A new monopoly earns $10 million a year in profit, and its deadweight triangle is $5 million. Rivals can freely compete to own it. Up to how much could it cost society each year?
The raider must build a $200,000 pier it can never sell. The ferry charges $30. Does the raider come in?
choices: No: it would face a fare war it can't escape

quiz.question: Which seller is closest to a contestable market?
choices: The only railway into a city

quiz.question: A small airport's only airline charges high fares. Which change would most likely make it cut them?
choices: Rivals can rent gates month by month

quiz.question: A town's broadband cable is laid in the ground. If a rival laid a second one, what would the incumbent most likely do?
The monopoly town starts 2% poorer but grows 1.5% a year instead of 1%. How long until it is ahead?
A patent lets an inventor charge far above cost for twenty years. What is the law trading?
choices: Lower prices today for faster innovation later
Faster innovation today for lower prices later
Nothing: a patent removes the deadweight loss

quiz.question: A monopoly costs 5% of output today and adds 0.1 percentage points of growth a year. Roughly how long until it pays off?
A museum used to charge everyone €15. Now tourists pay €20 and locals €5. When is the new scheme more likely to be efficient?
choices: If more people visit in total

quiz.question: A drug firm sells the same pill for $1,000 in a rich country and $50 in a poor one. If buyers could resell pills across the border, what would the firm most likely do?
choices: Set one price, and maybe stop selling in the poor country

quiz.question: A town has 300 cafés. One cuts its coffee price. Must it think about how the others react?
Two ferry companies share one route. One cuts its fare; the other matches the next day. What did the first one gain?
choices: Few new passengers, a lower fare on every ticket

quiz.question: Two airlines each pick a fare for one route. Which pair of fares is a Nash equilibrium?
choices: The pair that earns them most together
A pair where each fare is the best reply to the other's

quiz.question: Two Harbourtown bakeries each earn most if both price high, but each wins customers by undercutting, and no deal can be enforced. What do you expect?
Harbourtown's fishers agree a catch limit. What would most help them keep it?
choices: A council fine larger than the gain from cheating
Telling each that the others will cheat

quiz.question: Two Harbourtown fishers share the fishing grounds, and each could overfish. When is restraint most likely?
choices: One retires next month, and both know it
They'll fish side by side for decades
They sign a promise but never meet again

quiz.question: Why does a seller on a site with public reviews ship honestly to a buyer she'll never see again?
choices: Reviews tie each sale to all her future buyers
Honesty always pays in a one-off deal

quiz.question: Two neighbours play strict tit for tat. A greeting is missed by accident, and one thinks it was a snub. What follows?
Two online shops sell the identical charger. Shoppers compare prices on one site, and either shop can ship to everyone. Where do prices go?
Two cement firms each built one kiln that took years to build and now runs flat out. Their price is most likely…
choices: Above cost but below the monopoly price

quiz.question: Which cartel is most likely to last?
choices: Three salt makers with public weekly price lists, selling to many small shops
Twenty builders bidding in secret for one big bridge contract a decade

quiz.question: A free map app with 95% of users doubles its ads, and almost nobody leaves. What does a price-only test conclude?
choices: No harm: the price is still zero

quiz.question: A ride app charges drivers no commission for a year to sign them up. Is that clearly predatory?
choices: Not by itself: platforms often price one side low
No: a price can never be predatory

quiz.question: A city's biggest food-delivery app has most of its diners and restaurants. Which remedy keeps that network but adds competition?
choices: Split it into two delivery apps
Make it let rival apps take orders from its diners
Cap how many restaurants it lists

quiz.question: Where does the town's true cost of a hull sit?
choices: $350 above it, only at the last hull

quiz.question: A homeowner restores the old façade of her house on a historic street. Everyone who walks past enjoys it; nobody pays her. Left alone, the market gives…
The council overshoots: $1,000 a hull, twice the harm. Compared with no tax at all, the town is…
Each extra car trip into a city centre does $3 of harm to others, at the efficient number of trips. What charge per trip?
A government guesses carbon's harm at $50 a tonne, but the true harm is $150. With a $50 tax, emissions are…
For which pollutant is one national tax rate closer to right?
choices: Carbon dioxide, which does the same harm wherever it is released
Soot, which harms only the people nearby

quiz.question: Ann's tree blocks Ben's view. The law lets Ann keep it. The tree is worth $300 to Ann, the view $1,000 to Ben, and they talk easily. What happens?
choices: The tree stays: the law protects it
Ben pays Ann to cut it down
Ann pays Ben to accept it

quiz.question: Now the law gives Ben the right to his view instead. What changes?
choices: The tree still goes, but Ann gets nothing for it
Ben must pay twice as much

quiz.question: A chemical in a lake is harmless up to a level and kills the fish above it. Cleanup costs are uncertain. Tax or quota?
A paper mill's cleanup costs are known to the cent, and so is the harm downstream. Tax or quota?
choices: Either: they land on the same point

quiz.question: A town wants a New Year's fireworks show, seen from every street, paid for by voluntary donations. What happens?
choices: They raise less than the show is worth
They raise more, since everyone enjoys it

quiz.question: A TV channel broadcasts free over the air: anyone with an aerial can watch. How can a private firm pay for it?
choices: Sell the viewers' attention to advertisers

quiz.question: A patent makes a new idea excludable. By Samuelson's argument, what is still lost?
choices: Uses by people who value it but won't pay the price

quiz.question: Forty farmers share an aquifer and can pump unseen at night. What most helps them keep a limit they agreed?
choices: A meter on every pump, read by the farmers
A bigger fine, but no meters
A leaflet on the falling water table

quiz.question: Thousands of satellites from many countries crowd low orbit, and every piece of debris endangers all. What does Ostrom's list say is missing?
choices: Few users who meet again and can watch each other
Nothing: space is too big to crowd

quiz.question: Mainland buyers can't tell Harbourtown's fresh fish from old, so all fish get one price. Whose catch leaves the market first?
A website for second-hand phones starts paying for an independent check of every phone. What happens to the average phone on sale?
Which market is most at risk of unravelling?
choices: A used boat engine from a stranger

quiz.question: Car insurers price by age, driving record and car. Why does adverse selection bite less there than in health?
choices: They see much of the risk and price it
Drivers don't know how they drive
Crashes are too rare to matter

quiz.question: A country makes insurers sell to anyone at one price, any time, with no mandate. What happens?
choices: People wait until they're sick to buy, and premiums climb
The healthy buy early to lock in a price

quiz.question: Renters drive rental cars harder than their own cars. What is that?
A car insurer wants fewer claims for small scratches but full cover for a wreck. Which design?
Harbourtown's insurer pays the full value of any boat lost at sea. Which of these is moral hazard?
choices: Fishers with the oldest boats buy the most cover
Insured fishers skip checking their moorings before a storm
The insurer raises premiums after a bad year

quiz.question: Which purchase can online reviews help you with least?
choices: A hotel room for next weekend
A pill that claims to cut your heart risk in 20 years

quiz.question: You are buying a used fishing boat and want its hull surveyed. Whose surveyor is most likely to tell you the truth?
choices: One the seller chooses and pays

quiz.question: Too few taxis at night. A councillor: 'The market fails, so the council must set taxi numbers.' What does the argument skip?
choices: How a real taxi rule would do

quiz.question: Say private broadband reaches 7 homes in 10. A council network promises all 10; real ones elsewhere reached about 8, late. What should the town compare?
choices: 7 against what a real council network would deliver

quiz.question: 'Governments are slow and get captured, so leave vaccination entirely to the market.' What is the flaw?
choices: Vaccines are not sold in markets
It compares a real state with a perfect market

quiz.question: A power plant's smoke cannot be taxed. Electric heaters run on its power. What should happen to heaters?
Say each car downtown does $4 of jam that can't be tolled. A park-and-ride lot at the edge pulls in new users, but only 1 in 4 of them would have driven downtown. Roughly what subsidy per user?
A monopolist already makes too little, and its smoke is untaxed. Is a tax equal to the full harm of the smoke the best tax?
choices: Not necessarily: a smaller one may be better

quiz.question: A city taxes plastic carrier bags, and shoppers buy more plastic bin liners instead. Compared with the harm of a bag, the best bag tax is…
A planner sets a tax of 30. The best tax turns out to be 18. Is her tax still better than no tax?
A region taxes petrol, but drivers fill up across the border. What most cuts how much the planner must know?
choices: Tax petrol in the neighbouring region too
Measure the harm of petrol more precisely

quiz.question: A health ministry ships the same yearly medicine order to every clinic. Some run out, others throw stock away. The officials are honest. What failed?
choices: Incentives: someone gains from the waste
Dispersed knowledge: each clinic's needs are local
Unknowable knowledge: nobody could know the needs

quiz.question: After 1973 US productivity growth slowed, but the central bank kept judging capacity by the old trend. If it was honest, what knowledge was missing?
choices: Changing: true once, stale by now

quiz.question: A city's honest planners keep drawing bus routes that few people ride. Which reform targets a knowledge failure?
choices: Try new routes on a few lines first and count the riders

quiz.question: Say a city plans a $200 million stadium subsidy: about $100 from each of 2 million taxpayers, all of it a gain for one team's owner. Who is more likely to lobby the council?
Who is most likely to read the details of a new fishing-quota law?
choices: A fisher whose catch depends on it
A shopper who buys fish every week
A voter in a very close election

quiz.question: Voters in a city all overestimate its crime rate, in the same direction. If turnout doubles, does the policy error shrink?
choices: No: the errors lean one way
Yes: the informed voters tip it

quiz.question: Which reform fits public choice best?
choices: Every subsidy expires unless the council votes for it again

quiz.question: Suppose a state's board of licensed beauticians writes the rules for hair braiding. Which rule does capture theory predict?
choices: Braiders must complete a long beauty-school course
Braiding needs no licence at all

quiz.question: A bank supervisor's examiners often leave to work for the banks they examined. Which rule aims straight at that channel?
choices: A waiting period before an examiner may join a bank she examined

quiz.question: Which reform most directly weakens capture of a licensing board?
choices: Officials who are not practitioners must approve its actions

quiz.question: The board sets each mill's target from the costs its manager reports, and pays a bonus for meeting the target. What cost does the manager report?
